flexor digitorum superficialis: Muscle whose four tendons insert into the middle phalanges; flexes the PIP joints. Median nerve.
flexor hallucis longus: Flexes the big toe and provides power during push-off; its tendon passes beneath the sustentaculum tali.
flexor pollicis longus: Runs from the front of the radius to the distal phalanx of the thumb; flexes the tip of the thumb. With anterior interosseous nerve damage the 'OK' sign cannot be made.
flexor retinaculum of ankle: Band between the medial malleolus and the calcaneus roofing the tarsal tunnel; the tibial nerve and posterior tibial artery pass beneath it (tarsal tunnel syndrome).
flexor retinaculum of wrist: Flexor retinaculum of wrist (transverse carpal ligament)
Strong band forming the roof of the carpal tunnel; the median nerve and nine flexor tendons pass beneath it. It is divided in carpal tunnel surgery.
foramen caecum of frontal bone: Small hole in front of the frontal crest; an emissary vein from the nose to the superior sagittal sinus may pass through it.
foramen magnum: Large opening in the skull base; the medulla, the vertebral arteries and the spinal roots of the accessory nerve (XI) pass through it.
foramen ovale: Oval hole in the greater wing; the mandibular nerve (V3) passes through it.
foramen rotundum: Round hole in the greater wing; the maxillary nerve (V2) passes through it.
foramen spinosum: Small hole in the greater wing; the middle meningeal artery passes through it.
foramen transversarium: Hole in the cervical transverse processes; the vertebral artery passes through it from C6 to C1.
fossa for lacrimal gland: Fossa in the anterolateral part of the orbital roof; the orbital part of the lacrimal gland lies in it.
fourth metacarpal bone: The 4th of the five long bones of the metacarpus; its base articulates with the carpal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
fourth metatarsal bone: The 4th of the five long bones of the metatarsus; its base articulates with the tarsal bones and its head with the proximal phalanx.
fourth rib: 4th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.
fovea for ligament of head of femur: Pit on the femoral head; the ligament of the head of the femur and the small artery within it enter here.
frenula capsulae: Synovial folds of the capsule reflected onto the femoral neck; they carry the retinacular vessels that supply the femoral head.
frontal bone: Bone forming the forehead, the roofs of the orbits and most of the anterior cranial fossa; it contains the frontal sinus. It joins the parietal bones at the coronal suture.
frontal border of parietal bone: Border forming the coronal suture with the frontal bone.
frontal crest: Midline ridge on the inner surface of the frontal bone; the falx cerebri attaches to it.
frontal eminence: Prominence on each side of the forehead; the site of the ossification centre at birth.
frontal margin of greater wing: Margin that articulates with the frontal bone.
frontal part of orbital margin: Part of the frontal bone forming the upper margin of the orbit.
frontalis muscle: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead; temporal branch of the facial nerve. In central facial palsy the forehead is spared, in peripheral palsy it is involved.
genioglossus muscle: Fan-shaped muscle forming the main mass of the tongue; supplied by the hypoglossal nerve, it protrudes the tongue. In unilateral paralysis the tongue deviates to the paralysed side.
geniohyoid muscle: Suprahyoid muscle from the mental spines on the inner surface of the mandible to the hyoid; supplied by C1, it pulls the hyoid forwards and upwards.
genion: Tip of the mental spines; an anthropometric landmark.
glabella: Smooth area between the eyebrows; a reference point in anthropometric measurement.
glenoid fossa: Shallow fossa forming the shoulder joint with the humeral head; deepened by the labrum.
glenoid labrum: Fibrocartilaginous ring on the rim of the glenoid cavity; deepens the socket. An anteroinferior tear is a Bankart lesion, a superior tear a SLAP lesion.
glenoid process of scapula: Lateral angle carrying the glenoid cavity.
gluteal surface of ilium: Outer surface of the ilium; the gluteal muscles arise here.
gluteal tuberosity: Rough area on the upper posterior surface of the femur; the deep fibres of gluteus maximus attach here.
gluteus maximus muscle: The largest muscle in the body; extends and laterally rotates the hip, and is active in climbing stairs and rising from sitting. Inferior gluteal nerve.
gluteus medius muscle: Runs from the outer surface of the ilium to the greater trochanter; abducts the hip and stabilises the pelvis during walking. With superior gluteal nerve damage a Trendelenburg sign appears.
gluteus minimus muscle: Fan-shaped muscle beneath gluteus medius; abducts and medially rotates the hip. Superior gluteal nerve.
gnathion: Lowest anterior point of the chin; an anthropometric landmark.
gracilis muscle: Long thin adductor running from the pubis to the pes anserinus; it also flexes the knee. Obturator nerve; used in flap and graft surgery.
greater horn of hyoid bone: Large horn projecting backwards from the body; felt on both sides when examining the throat.
greater sciatic foramen: Greater sciatic foramen; piriformis, the sciatic nerve and the gluteal vessels and nerves pass through it.
greater sciatic notch: Large notch on the posterior border of the ilium; ligaments convert it into the greater sciatic foramen.
greater trochanter: Large projection at the upper lateral end of the femoral neck; gluteus medius, minimus and piriformis attach to it, and it is felt on the side of the hip.
greater tubercle: Large prominence on the lateral side of the humeral head; supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor attach to it.
greater wing: Large wing of the sphenoid extending laterally; forms part of the middle cranial fossa and the lateral wall of the orbit.
groove for marginal sinus: Groove for the marginal sinus around the foramen magnum.
groove for middle meningeal artery: Branching groove on the inner surface; the middle meningeal artery runs in it, and fractures here cause an extradural haematoma.
groove for occipital sinus: Groove for the occipital sinus along the internal occipital crest.
groove for popliteus muscle: Groove on the outer surface of the lateral condyle; the popliteus tendon lies here.
groove for spinal nerve: Groove on the upper surface of a cervical transverse process; the spinal nerve runs in it.
groove for subclavius muscle: Groove on the lower surface of the shaft; subclavius attaches here.
groove for tendon of flexor hallucis lon: Groove for flexor hallucis longus tendon (calcaneus)
Groove beneath the sustentaculum tali; the flexor hallucis longus tendon passes here.
groove for transverse sinus: Horizontal groove on the inner surface; the transverse sinus runs in it and the tentorium cerebelli attaches to it.
groove for ulnar nerve: Groove behind the medial epicondyle; the ulnar nerve runs superficially here ('funny bone').
groove for vertebral artery: Groove on the upper surface of the posterior arch; the vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve (C1) run here.
groove of pterygoid hamulus: Groove of the pterygoid hamulus; the tensor veli palatini tendon turns around it.
grooves for extensor tendons: Grooves on the lower posterior surface of the radius; the extensor tendons pass through them.
